This March, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed it had no plans to launch a new generation of Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg published a new report today, further revealing Apple's strategic plans for the Mac Pro, including an unexpected development project…

The Inside Story of Apple Shelving the Mac Pro

Mark Gurman noted in the latest issue of his Power On newsletter that, internally at Apple, discontinuing the Mac Pro was 'never a predetermined course of action.' Gurman also revisited an earlier rumour: Apple had originally planned to follow up its 'Ultra' chip with a higher-end chip called 'Extreme.'

The report quoted: 'Apple is said to have previously developed two chips, the M2 Extreme and the M3 Extreme, but ultimately shelved the projects due to cost and demand considerations.'

As for the Mac Pro hardware that was in development, Gurman said Apple had two models (with internal codenames J170 and J190) that never officially launched.

The most intriguing part of the report is that one of them actually used an Intel processor:

Apple officially discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its website, and directed consumers to the Mac Studio instead. The ending was not entirely unexpected, but for loyal Mac Pro supporters, it still marks the end of an era.

What are your thoughts on Apple's decision to abandon the Mac Pro product line and instead bet on 'Extreme' chips in the Apple Silicon era? Feel free to share your views in the comments.
